meta.title: Charlotte-Area Young Adult Resource Navigator
meta.description: A researched working directory of reputable resources in Charlotte, surrounding communities within roughly 30 miles, and essential statewide or national fallback programs.
meta.radiusDefinition: Local results are grouped by service location within roughly 30 road miles of Uptown Charlotte. This is a practical service-area screen, not a precise geospatial guarantee.

triage.situation: Immediate danger, overdose, violence or serious injury
triage.backup: Use Safe Alliance, trafficking or crisis resources after immediate safety is addressed.
triage.limit: Do not use a routine referral process for an active emergency.

triage.situation: Suicidal thoughts or acute mental-health crisis
triage.limit: Call 911 when there is immediate danger or a medical emergency.

triage.situation: Homeless tonight or unsafe place to sleep
triage.backup: Ages 16–24: The Relatives On Ramp; men: Roof Above; women/children: Center of Hope.
triage.limit: Beds and housing are limited; assessment does not guarantee placement.

triage.backup: Ask about VPA, GEAR Up, Medicaid and foster-specific education funds.
triage.limit: Many benefits end at 21; act quickly.

triage.backup: Use NC 211 and Mecklenburg Community Resource Centers for additional benefits.
triage.limit: Call before traveling; hours and capacity change.

triage.backup: Call 911 for immediate danger; Legal Aid/Charlotte Legal Advocacy for civil legal help.
triage.limit: Protect confidential location and contact information.

triage.situation: No food or basic household items
triage.firstAction: Apply for SNAP and contact Nourish Up
triage.backup: Crisis Assistance Free Store; Second Harvest food locator.
triage.limit: Emergency food should be paired with a longer-term benefits plan.

triage.situation: LGBTQ+ young adult needs affirming housing/support
triage.backup: The Relatives housing and Coordinated Entry.
triage.limit: Program age ranges and housing openings vary.

fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Independent-living planning, funds, education and housing support
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Refer immediately and document the young adult's custody/discharge history

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Former foster youth no longer in county custody; confirm eligibility
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Post-custody transition support and eligible funding

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Must meet state criteria and complete a voluntary agreement
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Continued placement, case management and financial support
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Ask before discharge from care; do not wait until after the 18th birthday

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Mecklenburg youth aging out; pilot criteria
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Call LINKS and verify active enrollment/funding

fosterPrograms.program: Medicaid for Former Foster Care Youth
fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Former foster-care and Medicaid history rules apply
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: State former-foster status explicitly on application

fosterPrograms.ageWindow: Often under 26 for eligible former foster youth
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Confirm plan assignment and current contact information

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Aged out at 18 or adopted after 12; NC public school; at least half time
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: FAFSA + NC Reach application before enrollment

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Current/former foster youth and some adopted/guardianship youth
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Up to program limit for approved education costs
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Coordinate ETV, financial aid and LINKS

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Leaving foster care; local program criteria
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Request Charlotte-area referral and verify openings

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Mecklenburg young people; foster history not required
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Youth-centered case management and broad resource access
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Use as a central warm-handoff hub

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Homeless, at risk or fleeing violence; screening applies

fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Coordinate to avoid duplicate or conflicting mentor roles
Invite young adults who want peer voice and connection

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Federal foster-youth and homelessness criteria; local partnership required
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Time-limited housing voucher and supportive services
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Treat as a lead until LINKS/INLIVIAN confirms local pathway

fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Help obtaining IDs and vital documents

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Transitioning from foster care or adolescence; confirm current enrollment
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Mentoring, coaching, leadership, financial literacy and independent-living skills
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Ask about the current weekly virtual group and age-appropriate coaching track

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young women aging out of foster care; current program screening required
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Workshops, supportive relationships and transition-to-adulthood connection
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Verify current programming and do not promise residential housing

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Currently in foster care through Mecklenburg or Union County
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Committed adult mentor before the transition out of care
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Use for pre-age-out planning and coordinate clearly with any program mentor

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Foster-care or emancipated student interested in Livingstone College
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Foster-specific college recruitment and support pathway developed with Home4Me
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Contact the project before application and confirm current financial, housing and retention supports

needsMap.primaryOptions: Coordinated Entry; The Relatives Housing; Crisis Assistance Ministry
needsMap.strategy: Use Coordinated Entry for homelessness, but pursue prevention funds before eviction whenever possible.

needsMap.primaryOptions: SNAP/FNS; Nourish Up; Hearts & Hands; Hope Street; Crisis Assistance Free Store
needsMap.backupOptions: Second Harvest locator; Kingdom Kitchen; Hickory Grove Clothes Closet; Roof Above Day Services
needsMap.strategy: Pair emergency food with a benefits application so the plan is not pantry-dependent.

needsMap.primaryOptions: NCWorks NextGen; Goodwill Career Center; Urban League; OMITT Trade School
needsMap.backupOptions: BuildStrong Academy; She Built This City; Road to Hire; Year Up; Vocational Rehabilitation
needsMap.strategy: Choose one primary workforce coach to reduce duplicated plans and missed appointments.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Central Piedmont GED/CCR; NC Reach; ETV
needsMap.backupOptions: Library College & Career Prep; UNC Charlotte Niner Needs
needsMap.strategy: Foster-specific education funds have strict age/status requirements; verify before registration.

needsMap.primaryOptions: CATS fares/passes; MTS for eligible trips
needsMap.strategy: Build a route and monthly transit budget before accepting a job or school schedule.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Teen Health Connection; Care Ring; Charlotte Community Health Clinic
needsMap.backupOptions: C.W. Williams; Camino; county clinic directory
needsMap.strategy: Establish a medical home rather than relying on emergency departments.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Teen Health Connection; Mental Health America counseling; Alliance Health; Santé Mobile Crisis
needsMap.backupOptions: Barnabas Center; NAMI Charlotte; Time Out Youth; C.W. Williams
needsMap.strategy: Use 988/911 for crisis; routine therapy access often requires insurance and waitlist planning.

needsMap.backupOptions: Alliance Health; Roof Above wellness services
needsMap.strategy: Match the level of care to a clinical assessment; do not treat a peer mentor as treatment.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Mecklenburg DCR; Community Resource Centers; NC 211
needsMap.strategy: Track application date, case number, documents requested and appeal deadlines.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Common Wealth Charlotte; Crisis Assistance coaching
needsMap.strategy: Use counseling before high-cost loans or debt-consolidation products.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Mecklenburg Vital Records; I Am Here hotline
needsMap.strategy: Start early; missing identity documents can block work, housing, benefits and school.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Charlotte Center for Legal Advocacy; Legal Aid NC
needsMap.strategy: Legal deadlines are unforgiving; make the referral as soon as notice or court papers appear.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Child Care Resources; WIC; Nurse-Family Partnership
needsMap.backupOptions: Smart Start; Crittenton; Charlotte Family Housing
needsMap.strategy: Child care subsidy and actual provider placement are separate steps.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Safe Alliance; National Human Trafficking Hotline
needsMap.strategy: Use survivor-led safety planning and protect confidential location/contact information.

needsMap.primaryOptions: program mentor; Home4Me LEG Up on LIFE; Charlotte Angels; SaySo
needsMap.backupOptions: CFK Mentor Match for youth under 18; Time Out Youth; Step Up to Leadership; faith/community partners
needsMap.strategy: Define roles clearly. One consistent relational through-line is more valuable than several helpers giving competing direction.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Mecklenburg LINKS; Home4Me LEG Up on LIFE; City JCRT; The Relatives On Ramp
needsMap.backupOptions: Community Culinary School; Per Scholas; Common Heart; Charlotte Area Fund; Goodwill/NCWorks
needsMap.strategy: Choose the program that lets the young adult practice the skill in a real setting. Avoid sending someone to several overlapping classroom-style programs at once.

partnerships.whyStrategic: Highest-leverage youth hub for ages 16–24; housing and broad case management
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Create a named referral contact and two-way warm-handoff process
partnerships.referralPathway: Referral form, consent, response-time expectation, status updates

partnerships.whyStrategic: Gateway to foster-specific benefits with hard age cutoffs
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Quarterly eligibility case review for young adults under 21
partnerships.referralPathway: Release, eligibility checklist, age-out deadline alerts

partnerships.whyStrategic: Evidence-informed intensive transition support for eligible foster youth
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Clarify referral criteria and how LifeSet and program mentorship can coexist
partnerships.referralPathway: Referral source, duplication boundaries, case communication

partnerships.whyStrategic: Required gateway for much of the homelessness system
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Learn the assessment process and escalation path for youth
partnerships.referralPathway: Call workflow, documents, consent, callback tracking

partnerships.whyStrategic: Core eviction-prevention and essential-goods resource
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Establish document checklist and a referral contact
partnerships.referralPathway: Landlord/utility documents, appointment process, outcome feedback

partnerships.whyStrategic: Age-aligned integrated medical and behavioral care through 25
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Create a direct appointment/referral workflow
partnerships.referralPathway: Consent, insurance, no-show rescheduling, crisis boundary

partnerships.whyStrategic: Safety-net primary care and first-time-parent home visiting
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Clarify uninsured referral and fee documentation
partnerships.referralPathway: Eligibility documents, appointment lead times, follow-up

partnerships.whyStrategic: Benefits, housing, health and civil legal issues commonly block stability
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Request staff training on issue spotting and urgent deadlines
partnerships.referralPathway: Intake categories, emergency escalation, document transfer

partnerships.whyStrategic: Age-specific workforce services and supportive funding
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Create a shared employment referral checklist
partnerships.referralPathway: Eligibility documents, assigned coach, attendance expectations

partnerships.whyStrategic: Budgeting, credit and safe financial products fit the program's independence goals
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Arrange recurring financial-counseling slots or workshops
partnerships.referralPathway: Consent, attendance, coaching scope, loan boundaries

partnerships.whyStrategic: Local continuum for substance-use assessment and treatment
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Define assessment and urgent detox referral steps
partnerships.referralPathway: Clinical confidentiality, transportation, payment, discharge coordination

partnerships.whyStrategic: Child care is a frequent barrier to work and school for young parents
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Create subsidy plus provider-search referral workflow
partnerships.referralPathway: Documents, waitlist, approved activity, provider placement

partnerships.whyStrategic: Affirming housing, counseling and community for LGBTQ+ young adults
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Establish a confidential specialist referral relationship
partnerships.referralPathway: Consent, privacy, housing/therapy waitlists, role boundaries

partnerships.whyStrategic: Critical safety partner for domestic violence and sexual assault
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Request trauma-informed referral and safety-planning training
partnerships.referralPathway: Confidential contact method, emergency versus non-emergency, releases

partnerships.whyStrategic: Disability can affect work, transit, benefits and independent living
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Clarify when to refer to CIL versus vocational rehabilitation
partnerships.referralPathway: Disability documentation, goals, benefits counseling, employment plan

partnerships.whyStrategic: Primary local path for GED, adult education and affordable credentials
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Identify a navigator for former foster youth and directory referrals
partnerships.referralPathway: Placement testing, FAFSA, NC Reach/ETV, attendance support

partnerships.whyStrategic: Local foster-specific mentoring and life-skills support that complements the program relationships
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Clarify enrollment, age tracks and how individual coaching can complement a program mentor
partnerships.referralPathway: Eligibility, consent, meeting schedule, staff contact and progress communication

partnerships.whyStrategic: Career-readiness and soft-skills cohorts have served young adults through age 24
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Request a standing notification when JCRT or equivalent 16–24 cohorts open
partnerships.referralPathway: Age/residency criteria, application dates, attendance and completion follow-up

partnerships.whyStrategic: Combines employable skills, mentoring, life skills and placement in one structured pathway
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Learn admissions criteria, cohort dates and scholarship/funding process
partnerships.referralPathway: Application, interview, schedule, transportation, attendance and placement follow-up

partnerships.whyStrategic: No-cost technical training includes professional development and learner support
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Identify a recruitment contact and realistic readiness screen for directory referrals
partnerships.referralPathway: Course prerequisites, deadline, intensity, technology needs and support plan

partnerships.whyStrategic: Union County food access plus economic-empowerment and success-coaching programs
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Create a warm handoff for Union County young adults needing both crisis and growth support
partnerships.referralPathway: Residency, pantry access, class enrollment and coach communication

partnerships.organization: Mental Health America of Central Carolinas
partnerships.whyStrategic: Free counseling and navigation for uninsured or underinsured young adults in Mecklenburg and Cabarrus counties
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Create a warm-handoff process and confirm seasonal counseling-center capacity
partnerships.referralPathway: Eligibility, release, appointment timing, telehealth options and escalation when capacity is full

partnerships.whyStrategic: Foster-specific college pathway that may complement NC Reach, ETV and Home4Me support
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Clarify the current student support package and referral timeline
partnerships.referralPathway: Admission, financial aid, housing, mentoring, campus contact and ongoing student-status updates

partnerships.whyStrategic: Local hands-on trades training with career services and a welcoming entry model
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Identify current courses, tuition assistance and a realistic readiness screen
partnerships.referralPathway: Information session, funding, prerequisites, attendance, certification and job-placement support

partnerships.whyStrategic: Potential tuition-free construction training with mentoring and professional development
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Confirm whether the Charlotte academy is actively enrolling and when the next cohort begins
partnerships.referralPathway: Eligibility, enrollment contact, location, class schedule, credentials and employer connection

partnerships.whyStrategic: Equine-assisted mentoring and life-skills work aligns strongly with the program's relational farm vision
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Confirm whether participants age 18 or older can be served and explore a pilot partnership
partnerships.referralPathway: Age fit, goals, consent, mentor boundaries, scheduling, cost and progress communication

partnerships.whyStrategic: Low-barrier food, hygiene, baby and pet assistance with pickup and limited delivery
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Clarify referral scheduling and whether the program can assist with appointment coordination
partnerships.referralPathway: Appointment, ID/residence documents, delivery criteria, no-show rules and frequency
